value_text: construct=B. linens encapsulin; variant_status=wild_type; assembly_symmetry=icosahedral; T_number=1; T_number_basis=directly_reported; shell_subunit_count=60; shell_diameter_nm=22.8; wall_thickness_nm=2.8-3.0; inner_volume_A3=~2.6 × 10^6; curated_notes=Canonical cargo-free WT T=1 assembly. Putri et al. 2017 directly characterized nonloaded B. linens encapsulin (nl-E) as an icosahedral T=1 shell with an outer diameter of 22.8 nm and an average shell thickness of 2.8-3.0 nm; the internal volume of the B. linens encapsulin particle was reported as ~2.6 × 10^6 Å^3. The inner diameter was reported to be identical to the DyP- and TFP-loaded maps, but no separate numerical inner-diameter value was given, so inner_diameter_nm is left blank. Native mass spectrometry in Snijder et al. 2016 directly detected the cargo-free 60-mer and lower-abundance assembly species. PDB 7BCV / EMD-12144 provides a 2.28 Å high-resolution cryo-EM structure of the recombinant apo shell and is an icosahedral homo-60-mer; Cuthbert et al. 2024 independently refers to 7BCV as apo-Enc. The nl-E preparation could contain nonspecifically packaged cellular material in a subset of particles, but no defined cognate cargo was present. The 30-mer, 58-mer and other lower-order species observed by native mass spectrometry are not treated as separate assemblies because they were not established as stable, structurally characterized nanocage states.
